m: उद्-घात m. the act of striking, wounding, inflicting a hurt
a thing begun, Ragh.; Kum.; Kathās.
breathing through the nostrils (as a religious exercise), VāyuP.
a division of a book, chapter, section, L.
a: उद्घातः — 1 Beginning, commencement; उद्घातः प्रणवो यासां Ku. 2. 12; आकुमारकथोद्घातं शालिगोप्यो जगुर्यशः R. 4. 20. --2 Allusion, reference; कथोद्घाताः U. 2. --3 Striking, wounding, inflicting an injury. --4 A stroke, blow, wound. --5 Tripping, slipping, jolting, shaking (as of a carriage); ययावनुद्घातसुखेन सोऽध्वना Śi. 12. 2; R. 2. 72; Ve. 2. 28; चक्र˚ V. 1; U. 5. 1. --6 Rising, elevation. --7 A club, mallet. --8 A weapon (in general). --9 Breathing through the nostrils as a religious exercise (Wilson). --10 A division of a book, chapter; section.

m: उद्-घातक and उद्-घात्य, n. a dialogue carried on in short abrupt but significant words, Pratāpar.; Daśar.
उद्-घातन n. a bucket for drawing (water), L.
उद्घातिन् mfn. having elevations, uneven, rough (v.l. for उत्-खातिन्), Śak. 10, 6.
a: उद्घातिन् — a. Uneven, rough.

m: उद्-घात्यक m. abrupt interruption in the prologue of a drama (where an actor suddenly strikes in with an irrelevant remark caused by his having mistaken a word uttered by another actor), Sāh. 289.

a leather bucket used for drawing up water, L.

उद्घटितं — A hint.

m: उद्-√ घट्ट् Caus. -घट्टयति and -घाट्टयति, to unlock, open, L.; to stir up, Car.

उद्घट्टित — a. 1 Opened, unlocked. --2 Separated; Śi. 11. 42.

a: उद्घृष्टं — A peculiar fault in pronunciation.

उद्-घोष—डिण्डिम m. a drum beaten by a town-crier (to attract attention in the streets), Kathās.
